text: Is AI drinking the planet dry?
This is an AI data center. And you see, its chips run so hot they have to drink to survive.
Inside: racks of GPUs. One rack pulls a hundred and twenty kilowatts.
Air can't keep up. So the cooling goes straight to the chip.
Cold plates sit on every GPU. Coolant flows through, and carries the heat away.
That loop dumps its heat into a chiller. Then up to the roof.
Cooling towers. This is where water is lost. It evaporates, and the heat leaves as vapour.
How much? Operators measure litres per kilowatt-hour. Amazon reports zero point one five. Microsoft, zero point two seven.
But that's only half the bill. Power plants drink too. In America, that hidden water is twelve times bigger.
So, one prompt? Google says about five drops.
One big data center? Up to five million gallons a day.
The fixes? Closed loops that never evaporate. Dry coolers instead of towers. And cooler climates.
Of course, one question won't drain a river. But billions a day? That adds up.
What should we take apart next?
